categories.name: Red Hat & Linux
categories.tagline: Official Red Hat courseware from an authorized partner.
categories.intro: Build enterprise Linux skills from first command to RHCE, then extend into OpenShift and OpenStack. IT Security Nepal has delivered Red Hat training as an authorized partner for more than 15 years.
objectives: Administer Red Hat Enterprise Linux systems, users, storage and services
Prepare for the RHCSA (EX200) and RHCE (EX294) performance-based exams
Automate administration at scale with Ansible
Run containers and Kubernetes workloads on Red Hat OpenShift

faqs.q: Which Red Hat course should I start with?
faqs.a: Start with RH124 (Red Hat System Administration I). It assumes no prior Linux experience and is the first step toward RHCSA, followed by RH134.

faqs.q: Do I need RHCSA before RHCE?
faqs.a: Yes. RHCE (RH294) builds on RHCSA-level skills, so complete RH124 and RH134 first.

faqs.q: Is the training based on official Red Hat material?
faqs.a: Yes. As a Red Hat Authorized Training Partner, our Red Hat courses use official courseware and labs.

categories.name: Cybersecurity & Ethical Hacking
categories.tagline: From SOC fundamentals to advanced penetration testing.
categories.intro: Learn to defend, detect and ethically attack systems in a hands-on lab. Programmes range from the beginner-friendly Junior Security Analyst Track to expert-level ethical hacking and penetration testing.
objectives: Understand attacker methodology, from reconnaissance to post-exploitation
Analyse logs and investigate alerts the way a SOC analyst does
Run structured penetration tests and write actionable reports
Collect and preserve digital evidence for forensic investigations

faqs.q: I'm new to security. Where should I start?
faqs.a: The Junior Security Analyst Track is designed for beginners with basic computer knowledge and builds toward entry-level SOC roles.

faqs.q: What do I need before Ethical Hacking Expert?
faqs.a: An understanding of networking, IP addressing and Linux and Windows operating systems. A foundation course such as CompTIA Security+ is preferred.

categories.name: Networking & Cisco
categories.tagline: Routing, switching and enterprise network design.
categories.intro: Go from networking fundamentals to the enterprise core with Cisco-aligned training. Start with CCNA, then continue to CCNP-level ENCOR, ENARSI and data-centre technologies.
objectives: Configure and troubleshoot routers, switches and VLANs
Design and secure enterprise networks
Implement advanced routing and services
Prepare for Cisco certification exams

faqs.q: Do I need experience before CCNA?
faqs.a: No formal prerequisite is required, though basic computer and networking awareness helps. CompTIA Network+ is a good optional starting point.

categories.name: DevOps & Kubernetes
categories.tagline: CI/CD, containers and Kubernetes for modern teams.
categories.intro: Learn the tools and practices engineering teams use to ship software reliably: Git, CI/CD pipelines, containers, infrastructure automation and Kubernetes administration and security.
objectives: Build CI/CD pipelines and automate deployments
Containerise applications with Docker
Administer Kubernetes clusters (CKA)
Secure clusters and workloads (CKS)

faqs.q: Do I need Linux skills for DevOps?
faqs.a: Yes. DevOps Mastery covers Linux fundamentals, but prior Linux experience (for example RH124/RH134) makes the course much easier.

categories.name: Microsoft Azure & Cloud
categories.tagline: Administer, secure and design on Microsoft Azure.
categories.intro: Microsoft-aligned training for cloud administrators, architects, security analysts and data engineers, covering Azure, Microsoft 365, identity and security operations.
objectives: Administer Azure subscriptions, networking and storage
Design secure, scalable Azure infrastructure
Operate Microsoft security tooling and identity services
Build data pipelines on Azure

faqs.a: Most learners start with AZ-104 (Azure Administrator) before moving to design (AZ-305) or DevOps (AZ-400).

categories.name: CompTIA Certifications
categories.tagline: Vendor-neutral certifications, from A+ to CASP+.
categories.intro: Vendor-neutral CompTIA training for IT support, networking, Linux, cloud and security roles. A strong foundation for any IT career path.
objectives: Build core IT support and hardware skills (A+)
Understand networks and security fundamentals (Network+, Security+)
Progress to analyst and advanced practitioner roles (CySA+, PenTest+, CASP+)

faqs.q: Which CompTIA certification is right for beginners?
faqs.a: A+ for IT support roles, Network+ for networking, and Security+ as a first security certification.

categories.name: ISC2 Security Certifications
categories.intro: Preparation for globally recognised ISC2 credentials for experienced security professionals: CISSP for security leadership and CCSP for cloud security.
objectives: Master security and risk management principles
Design secure architectures for on-premises and cloud
Prepare for the CISSP and CCSP exams

faqs.a: CISSP is aimed at experienced security practitioners. ISC2 sets professional experience requirements for certification; check them before enrolling.

categories.name: Job-Ready Programs & Bootcamps
categories.intro: Short, intensive programmes that get you working on real systems fast: a five-day Linux Bootcamp, a Job-Ready Program for roles in Australia and New Zealand, and Graphic Designing with AI.
objectives: Gain job-ready technical skills in weeks, not semesters
Build a portfolio, resume and interview confidence
Prepare for the next certification on your path

faqs.q: Who is the Job-Ready Program for?
faqs.a: Students and fresh graduates who want to start an IT career in Australia or New Zealand.

faqs.q: When does the Linux Bootcamp run?
faqs.a: Monday to Friday, 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM (4 hours daily, 20 hours total). A new batch starts every Monday.

items.q: Do you provide training for complete beginners?
items.a: Yes. Courses are designed for learners at every stage, with a step-by-step approach so beginners build a strong foundation before moving to advanced topics. Good starting points are the Linux Bootcamp, RH124, CCNA, CompTIA A+ and the Junior Security Analyst Track.

items.q: How do I choose the right course?
items.a: Use the Course Finder or book free counselling. We look at your background and career goal and recommend a learning path, not just a single course.
Each course page lists its prerequisites. Many foundation courses only need basic computer skills; advanced courses build on earlier certifications.
Yes. Live Virtual Training runs in real time with an instructor. Classroom, one-on-one and flip-class formats are also available.
New batches start regularly. See Upcoming Batches for current schedules, or contact us for the next start date of a specific course.
Around 80% of class time is practical, lab-based work on real systems.

items.q: Are you an official Red Hat Training Partner?
items.a: Yes. IT Security Nepal has been a Red Hat Authorized Training Partner for over 15 years and delivers Red Hat courses with official courseware and labs.

items.q: Do you help with certification exams?
items.a: Yes. Courses are certification-focused and include exam guidance. Ask an advisor about exam registration for your certification.
Fees vary by course and training mode. Contact an advisor for current fees and any running offers.
Send an enquiry from any course page, call us, or visit our office in New Baneshwor. An advisor will confirm the batch, fees and payment options.
Yes. We design customised programmes for organisations in cybersecurity, DevOps, cloud and infrastructure, aligned with your team's goals and technologies.
